title: Geometry-Guided Representations for Coherent Lane and Traffic Topology Reasoning in Driving Scenes

problem.claim: Autonomous driving requires accurate perception of road elements and reasoning about lane connectivity and traffic regulation.

gap.claim: Existing methods fragment perception and topology reasoning and often omit geometric relationships during feature extraction, relying on brittle inference-time post-processing or coordinate heuristics.

contributions.claim: CoPo is a unified framework that integrates geometry-guided relational modeling across perception, topology reasoning, and supervision.
The framework uses geometry-biased self-attention and curve-guided cross-attention for lane detection, plus geometry-enhanced L2L and cross-view L2T topology heads.
A contrastive InfoNCE strategy regularizes relational embeddings, and the design supports end-to-end joint optimization of perception and reasoning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On OpenLane-V2, the authors report gains of +3.1 in DET_l, +5.3 in TOP_ll, +4.9 in TOP_lt, and +4.4 overall in OLS over existing methods.
The authors report that CoPo sets a new state-of-the-art on OpenLane-V2.

narrative_sequence.summary: Road topology reasoning is presented as fundamental to autonomous driving and requires perception plus connectivity understanding.
Prior approaches separate perception from topology reasoning and underuse geometry during feature extraction.
CoPo addresses the gap with geometry-guided relational modeling across perception, reasoning, and supervision.
The authors report substantial OpenLane-V2 improvements across detection, topology, and overall OLS metrics.

source_observation.claim: CoPo jointly models perception and topology using geometry-guided relational features and relational supervision.

interpretation.claim: Encoding task-relevant relational structure during representation learning may reduce dependence on brittle downstream heuristics.

application.claim: Structured scene-reasoning systems could consider end-to-end representations that incorporate geometric relations across detection and reasoning tasks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported driving-scene dataset and tasks.

unknowns: Detailed dataset composition, splits, and evaluation protocol are not specified.
Baseline identities and statistical variability of the reported gains are not specified.
Ablation results separating the three modeling levels are not specified.
Implementation details and reproducibility resources are not specified.
